exposure: Maternal origin (sub-Saharan Africa or South/Southeast Asia)
cohort: The study included 844,021 women with singleton vaginal deliveries in Sweden between 2005 and 2016, after excluding cesarean, forceps deliveries, and cases with missing data.
finding: A prediction model using antenatally available data was developed and validated to predict the risk of obstetrical anal sphincter injuries with moderate certainty, achieving an AUC of 0.79.
mod_finding: Vacuum extraction was identified as a factor that increased the risk of obstetrical anal sphincter injury.
birth_weight: N/A (birthweight was included as an exposure variable, not a selection criterion)
